title: Maximum Passive Stiffness Measurement in Mice
author: John Rutledge
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.yrtfv6n

steps.title: Anesthetize Mice
steps.instruction: Anesthetize mice using an intraperitoneal injection of pentobarbital at a dose of 50 mg/kg weight.

steps.title: Dissect and Prepare Arteries
steps.instruction: Dissect either the common carotid arteries or the aorta as described in the Macrovascular Permeability and Lipoprotein Flux protocol.

substeps.instruction: Option A: Use artery explants immediately for analysis.
Option B: Store explants in Krebs-Henseleit buffer at 4°C overnight.
Option C: Snap-freeze in liquid nitrogen and store at -80°C; thaw overnight in Krebs-Henseleit buffer at 4°C prior to analysis.

steps.title: Mount Arterial Segment
steps.instruction: Insert two stainless steel rods (200-µm outside diameter) in a parallel manner through the lumen of a 1-mm section of carotid artery while the vessel is immersed in Krebs-Henseleit buffer.

substeps.instruction: Attach one rod to a motorized controller.
Attach the second rod to a force transducer.

steps.title: Precondition Arterial Segments
steps.instruction: Precondition the arterial segments three times at approximately 10% of their maximal load.

steps.title: Measure Stiffness and Calculate Parameters
steps.instruction: Use the motorized controller to pull the rods apart and record vessel tension to generate stress (vessel tension development divided by vessel area, N/mm²) versus strain (vessel circumference) curves.

substeps.instruction: Calculate maximum strain (strain at vessel breakage).
Calculate maximal stress (vessel tension at maximum strain).
Calculate failure energy (area under the stress-strain curve).
Define Maximum Passive Stiffness (MPS) as the maximal slope of the load vs. strain relationship.

steps.title: Perform Replicates
steps.instruction: Perform the experiment on three 1-mm segments of each artery and average the results.
